why: The runtimes coai-mcp runs on a NATIVE Linux host (a Linux kernel that is not WSL), and for each the first coai-mcp release that does (E2 of research/PLAN_kimi_and_vibe_on_native_linux_E2.md, DN1) and WHY it is admitted: `basis`.

ONE file, read by BOTH sides: the server embeds it (CoaiMcp.Runners.native-linux-admission.json; HostAdmission.AdmittedOnNativeLinux IS its runtime names) and the extension's ON_NATIVE_LINUX_SINCE in src/runtimeSince.ts is held to it by its own test (nothing parses the other side's source).

A runtime with NO entry is REFUSED on a native Linux host: an absent fact refuses. An entry is added by an edit to THIS file. `basis` is `measured` (`source` names the RESULTS section whose cells are the evidence, and the runtime must also hold a confined, measured `linux` row in shared/consultant-limitations.json) or

`owner-decision` (the owner's decision of 2026-10-23, todo/PLAN_kimi_and_vibe_on_native_linux_E2.md, DN1 of E2: "unmeasured" is a NOTE, never a refusal). An owner-decision runtime runs WITHOUT a measurement, so it carries a one-sentence `note` the person is shown on its card and its launch (KimiLaunch.HostNote),

and its `linux` row in shared/consultant-limitations.json must say `unmeasured` and name the decision (a test holds both). Only a runtime whose launch carries that note may use `owner-decision` (today Kimi's). `since` is the next minor after the newest released src_mcp when the entry was made; whoever cuts the release keeps it level with the tag (DL14).

runtimes.source: The owner's decision of 2026-10-23 (todo/PLAN_kimi_and_vibe_on_native_linux_E2.md, DN1 of E2); E3's measurement is optional evidence, not a gate
runtimes.note: Kimi is not measured on a native Linux host; it is admitted here by the owner's decision of 2026-10-23, so what it can read or write here is not claimed.
